# A lock toggle restages the dock shell, so every header in the app repaints

## Context

Operator report on a downstream dock host (2026-09-03): clicking the lock action makes **every** tab-container header in the app flicker — "so I assume all of them update, for triggering an action that affects the content of its tab. serious no-go."

Reproduced and measured headless on the served app. The first sub of #18151: the seam where the engine's declining default is cheapest to fix and most visible.

## The Problem

`setItemLocked` sets one boolean on one item. It changes no node, no split, no edge zone. It nevertheless takes the **full staged transaction**, because `Workspace#getRefreshOptions(descriptor, source)` returns `{}` by default — documented as "the default takes the full staged transaction every time" — and a consumer that does not override it never gets anything narrower.

Measured, one lock click, MutationObserver over the whole app subtree:

```
TOTAL mutations           : 32
  inside a tab header     :  7   (the locked pane's own header)
  OUTSIDE any header      : 25
  on the dock host        :  4
distinct non-header targets: neo-dashboard-dock-split (childList add/remove pairs),
                             neo-dashboard-dock-edge-row, neo-dashboard-dock-edge-zone,
                             neo-body, dock-flip-item-*, neo-dashboard-dock-query-host
```

The mechanism is re-parenting, not re-creation — which is why it is easy to miss. Three earlier arms of mine found nothing: header DOM nodes are **retained** (object permanence holds — 3 of 3 survived a marker stamped on the node), and the surviving headers show zero internal mutations because `syncDock*Action` writes only on a value change. The churn is one level up: the splits and edge rows have their children removed and re-added, so every retained header is re-parented, and a re-parented node repaints. An observer scoped to the headers cannot see its own cause.

`{retainTopology}` — "in-place item reconciliation on a proven-identical structural shell" — is exactly the shape this operation needs, and nothing asks for it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` — `getRefreshOptions(descriptor, source) { return {} }`; the JSDoc names `{geometryOnly}` for a pure `resizeSplit`, `{retainTopology}` for item-only deltas, `{preserveItemIds}` for per-commit owner-held ids.
- `refreshDockWorkspace` reads `{geometryOnly=false, retainTopology=false}` from those options; `getReconcileOptions` can force `retainTopology` (`forcedRetainTopology ?? retainTopology`).
- `src/dashboard/dock/model/Operations.mjs` owns the whole vocabulary — `addTab`, `applyDocument`, `setActiveItem`, `moveItem`, `splitNode`, `moveNode`, `resizeSplit`, `resizeEdgeZone`, `detachItem`, `closeItem`, `setItemLocked`, `setItemPinned`, `setItemAutoHidden` — and is therefore the only place that can classify them honestly.
- `Workspace#handleDockLockAction` commits `setItemLocked` and calls `onDockZoneDocumentChange`, which schedules the refresh. The consumer under test overrides neither refresh hook, which is the intended-to-be-safe path.

## The Fix

Declare the change-class per operation as data beside the reducer that owns it, and let the engine derive the refresh shape from the descriptor it already receives. `setItemLocked`, `setItemPinned` and `setItemAutoHidden` are item-flag deltas; `resizeSplit` and `resizeEdgeZone` are geometry; the rest restructure. `getRefreshOptions` stays as the host override, now layered over a correct default rather than being the only source of truth.

The classification belongs in `model/Operations.mjs`, not in a `Workspace` switch: the reducer that implements an operation is what knows what it touched, and co-locating them is what keeps a new operation from silently defaulting to "restage everything" or, worse, to a wrong fast path.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| per-operation change-class | `src/dashboard/dock/model/Operations.mjs` | each operation declares `topology` / `geometry` / `itemFlags` beside its reducer | an operation without a declaration is treated as `topology` (today's behaviour) | JSDoc | one arm per class; an undeclared operation stays full-transaction |
| `Workspace#getRefreshOptions` | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` | derives from the descriptor's change-class; unchanged signature | a host override still wins outright | JSDoc | override-wins arm, mutation-proven |
| `refreshDockWorkspace` refreshOptions | same | unchanged contract (`geometryOnly` / `retainTopology` / `preserveItemIds`) | unchanged | JSDoc | existing arms stay green |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — the docking design record's projection and object-permanence rules are what this restores in practice; no authority changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A `setItemLocked` commit on a workspace that overrides no refresh hook mutates nothing outside the affected pane's own header — asserted as a mutation count over the whole app subtree, not as a screenshot.
- [ ] AC-2 Red-first: the same witness is red at the current head, reporting non-header mutations on the splits / edge rows. The witness must observe **above** the headers, since an observer scoped to the headers cannot see re-parenting.
- [ ] AC-3 Every operation in `model/Operations.mjs` carries a change-class; an operation with none is treated as topology-changing, and a witness proves that fallback for a synthetic undeclared operation.
- [ ] AC-4 `setItemPinned` / `setItemAutoHidden` rail round trips and `resizeSplit` / `resizeEdgeZone` keep their current behaviour, with the existing dock component suites green at exact head.
- [ ] AC-5 A host override of `getRefreshOptions` still wins over the derived default, mutation-proven.
- [ ] AC-6 Object permanence is unregressed: retained tab headers and panes keep component identity across a lock toggle, and a marker set on a header DOM node survives it.

## Out of Scope

- The recreate and vessel defaults — sibling seams under #18151.
- Any change to what lock *means* (content inert, structural verbs fail closed): presentation and policy are untouched.
- Consumer-side classification of operations, which is the layering defect #18151 names.

## Avoided Traps

- **Scoping the witness to the headers.** That is what made three of my own measurement arms report a clean result on a defect the operator could see: node identity survives, internal mutations are zero, and the cause sits one level up. Observe the app subtree.
- **A consumer-side `getRefreshOptions` switch.** It fixes one app, reproduces the defect in every other, and rots as the vocabulary grows.
- **Reading flicker as a repaint-only cosmetic.** The re-parenting is real DOM work on every commit; the visual flicker is the symptom, not the cost.
- **Assuming `retainTopology` is safe for every non-topology operation.** It admits in-place reconciliation on a *proven-identical* shell; the declaration must come from the reducer, not from a guess about the operation's name.

## Related

- Sub of #18151 — the declining-default class this is the first instance of.
- #18014 AC-1/AC-7/AC-9 (closed) — the default action vector and the single-lifecycle-owner invariant.
- #18039 (closed) — the post-settle header sweep that walks the settled shell.
- ADR 0029 — docking design record.

`setItemAutoHidden: 'itemFlags'` turns it red.

- 2026-09-03T06:44:13Z @neo-opus-ada cross-referenced by #18159
- 2026-09-03T07:07:01Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `e42c3e3` - "test(dashboard): the preview-geometry arms wait for the projection to settle (#18152)

This is the arm that has been holding #18154 red, and it is mine — shipped in
#18146 and merged, so it has been able to fail on anyone's PR since.

`beforeEach` waited for the preview to attach and not for the projection to
settle. The reconciler stages the next shell as a hidden sibling before retiring
the old one, so for the duration of that transaction the host legitimately holds
two full-width shells and `scrollWidth` is 2x `clientWidth`. Measuring inside
that window reads a correct transient as the defect. It never reproduced across
ten local runs and failed twice on CI, which is a race against a slower machine
rather than a flaky suite — a distinction I got wrong earlier and was corrected
on.

The settle signal is deliberately NOT `scrollWidth`. That is the property both
arms exist to prove, and waiting for it would make them vacuous — passing
because the fixture eventually reached the state they claim to assert. Child
count is independent: the host holds its shell plus two persistent overlays at
rest, one more while a second shell is staged.

Full component suite 230 passed twice back to back at CI's own scope."

comment states the contract it enforced — a new operation added to dispatch
without a class fails there rather than degrading silently.

`topology` is verified against the reducer rather than inferred from the name,
which matters because the name suggests it is only an `addTab` sibling. It is on
one branch; on the other it mints a node outright, and creating a node is
structural either way.

No behaviour change: an undeclared operation already fell through to `topology`,
so `getRefreshOptions` returned `{}` before and returns `{}` now. The entry stops
the two sibling maps drifting, which the dispatch table gets by construction and
a sibling map cannot inherit.

Full unit 3080 passed."
